The 283rd plenary meeting of the Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations is called to order. Distinguished delegates, this meeting has been convened to conclude the 2025 session of the Special Committee. And we will first take up Item 7, considerations of the draft report of the Working Group of the Whole.

In keeping with established practice, I will now update the Special Committee about the efforts of the Working Group of the Whole. Between Thursday, 20 February and Wednesday, 12 March, the Working Group of the Whole met to consider the draft recommendations of this session, and it did this through the format of its two sub-working groups. Regrettably, as you know, the Working Group was not able to reach consensus in its consideration of the draft conclusions and recommendations for this session. Therefore, The group does not have a substantive draft report this year. The working group acknowledged this outcome at the meeting it held just a few minutes ago.

Distinguished delegates, regarding the way forward, the facilitators and regional coordinators have proposed intercessional discussions in 2025. to be facilitated by the chair of the working group of the whole to consider the committee's working methods in relation to its annual report. I strongly believe that this will benefit our collective efforts to implement the important mandate which the General Assembly entrusted to the special committee. I recommend, therefore, that the Special Committee undertake intersessional discussions in 2025, facilitated by the Chair of the Working Group of the Whole, to consider the Committee's working methods in relation to its annual report. It is so decided. Distinguished delegates, we will now turn to agenda item 9, adoption of the report to the General Assembly at its 79th session. In that regard, a draft procedural report has been issued in all official languages as document A/AC.121/2021/1. 2025 backslash L.3, which has also been circulated to delegations via e-delegate. I now give the floor to the rapporteur of the Special Committee, Mr. Mohamed Soliman from Egypt, to briefly introduce the draft report. You have the floor.

Thank you, Mr. Chair, for giving me the floor. Good afternoon, dear colleagues, dear friends. Mr. Chair, distinguished members of the Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations, in my capacity as rapporteur of the Special Committee, I have the honor to introduce the draft report on the 2025 substantive session of the Special Committee as contained in document A/AC.121/2025/L.3. Section 1 of the report contains the introduction and request by the General Assembly that the Committee submit a report on its work at the current 79th session. Section 2 covers organizational matters, including the opening and duration of the session, election of officers, adoption of the agenda, organization of work, and proceedings of the Committee. Sections 3 and 4 refer to the outcome of the consideration of draft recommendations and conclusions by the Working Group of the Whole and to the adoption today of the draft report of the Special Committee for 2025. No section 5. The draft report of the Special Committee would normally include a section 5, comprising the entirety of the Special Committee's recommendations. Given the lack of consensus on those recommendations this session, section 5 of this draft report has been deleted. A list of the current members of the Special Committee is contained in document A/AC.121/2025/INF/3. With these few words, I recommend the draft report for adoption by the Special Committee. And let me end by expressing heartfelt thanks to the Chair, His Excellency Ambassador Michael Gort, for his able leadership and guidance throughout this session. I submit, Mr. Chair. Thank you.

I thank the rapporteur of the Special Committee for his statement. Distinguished delegates, may I take it that the Special Committee wishes to adopt the procedural report on its proceedings at its 2025 session as read out by the rapporteur? It is so decided. The procedural report of the Special Committee at its 2025 session is adopted. I would now like to open the floor to any member who wishes to make remarks at this time. kindly press your microphone button to request the floor. And in the interest of time, all speakers are requested to keep the remarks brief. I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Nigeria.

Thank you, Mr. Chair. Excellencies, distinguished delegates, ladies and gentlemen. The Nigerian delegation expresses deep appreciation to all delegations for their tireless engagements and commitment throughout this session and acknowledge the invaluable contributions of all negotiating teams, particularly those representing troop and police contributing countries, host nations, and regional coordinators. However, despite our collective efforts and good faith, negotiations, consensus on the 2025 C34 report could not be reached. Nevertheless, this outcome must not be seen as a setback, but rather as a reminder of the complexities of our work and the imperative to redouble our commitment to constructive dialogue. Mr Chair, The Special Committee remains the only United Nations forum mandated to comprehensively review all aspects of peacekeeping operations as stated in Resolution 19 of 2006. That is 60 years ago. Therefore, our work must remain insulated from extraneous political considerations that do not align with our core mandate of peacekeeping. Besides, The credibility and effectiveness of this committee depends on our ability to safeguard it as a space for meaningful, consensus-driven engagements. Towards this end, Nigeria reaffirms its unwavering support for UN peacekeeping and to the brave men and women who serve under the UN flag, as their safety, well-being, and operational effectiveness must remain central. Peacekeeping is not just a bureaucratic exercise, but about the safety, stability, and well-being of vulnerable populations. Therefore, our collective responsibility is to ensure that peacekeeping remains a reliable, adaptable, and effective tool for global security. The expectations of those we serve, the peacekeepers, host communities, and conflict-affected populations must remain our guiding principle. Nigeria welcomes the proposal for intercessional consultations on working methods, recognizing the importance of refining our approaches to ensure our deliberations continue the relevance and impact. These consultations could be instrumental in the future of peacekeeping operations currently being clamored for. We must protect the hard-won gains made over the years and ensure that previous agreements reflecting the collective wisdom of Member States are not undone in pursuit of short-term interests. Our progress in peacekeeping must be preserved and strengthened, not eroded. While this session has concluded without a consensus report, let this not signal division, but rather an opportunity for deeper engagement and renewed commitment. As Chair, Nigeria stands ready to work with all delegations in good faith to find practical solutions in the months ahead. We value our partnership and look forward to collaborating with you. The facilitation of intersessional consultations will be instrumental in identifying areas of improvement, enhancing our work methods, and preventing similar deadlocks in the future. Nigeria remains steadfast in its commitment to multilateralism, regional cooperation, and sustainable peace, and we look forward to continued dialogue and collaboration towards a stronger, more responsive UN peacekeeping framework. To conclude, Mr. Chair, let me also extend our appreciation and gratitude to the Secretariat for their tireless efforts in supporting our work. the interpreters, translators, and support staff for their hard work and dedication. As we close this session, I urge you all to remain committed to our shared vision of a more peaceful, prosperous, and equitable world, and continue to work together to make this vision a reality. I thank you, Mr. Chair.
I thank the distinguished representative of Nigeria, and I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Morocco.

Mr. Chair, allow me to start by expressing on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement our sincerest thanks to the Bureau, the Chair of the Working Group of the Whole, the all-women team of facilitators, Carla, Kulapa, Angie, and Elena, my fellow regional coordinators, and the Secretariat for your support and engagement during this session of the Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations, C-34. A special thank you to all the negotiators, particularly the Non-Aligned Movement negotiators team, for their tenacious efforts throughout the past three weeks. We deeply regret that despite engaging in good faith negotiations, we were unable to adopt a substantive report due to considerations that are not directly related to the core mandate of peacekeeping operations. Going forward, It is essential to ensure that our efforts to make peacekeeping more effective and efficient are no longer hindered by extraneous factors. We need to keep in mind the true essence of our mission and remind ourselves that we are working towards an objective far greater than national, than narrow political interests. Peacekeeping is about the safety, stability and well-being of vulnerable populations and our collective efforts must not sway from these goals. Mr. Chair, the Special Committee remains the only UN forum mandated to review the whole question of peacekeeping operations in all their aspects and for the improvement of peacekeeping. As such, we must all strive to safeguard it as a space where meaningful dialogue by Member States can take place, guided by the spirit of collective action, cooperation, consensus, and especially compromise. We must also recognize the importance of preserving the gains made in previous years regarding peacekeeping-related concepts. These concepts, which have been the result of many years of long and constructive consultations, represent the hard work and collective wisdom of Member States striving for the betterment of peacekeeping operations. It is essential that we do not lose sight of these valuable agreements, which have formed the foundation of our ongoing work. The progress we have made must be protected and built upon, not undone or disregarded in the pursuit of short-term national interests of some Member States, which undermine the collective interest of the whole membership. Maintaining these gains is key to ensuring the continued effectiveness and, most importantly, the credibility of peacekeeping efforts globally. Mr Chair, the C34 is also the only platform through which Member States, especially troop and police contributing countries, as well as host States, can actively contribute to discussions on peacekeeping-related issues. As the representative of the majority of these countries, the Non-Aligned Movement has consistently and will continue to insist that their contribution should be duly considered and taken into account, and not be seized hostage of the interests of few delegations which have access to other platforms that decide on peacekeeping-related matters. To conclude, Mr. Chair, and in light of the challenge we are sadly faced with today, though not deterred, we look forward to your crucial role in facilitating intercessional consultations among member states. These consultations should serve as an opportunity to reflect on our working methods, identify areas of improvement, and agree on practical solutions that can prevent the recurrence of situations where our work is unduly hindered. The C34 is a General Assembly subsidiary body, and we cannot allow to have vetoes in its decision making. The Chair's facilitation is vital to creating a constructive environment where member states can engage openly, transparently, and without obstacles. We are convinced that by enhancing our working methods and ensuring continuous dialogue, we can build a more effective and inclusive process for the future of peacekeeping. I thank you, Mr. Chair.
I thank the distinguished representative of Morocco, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Guatemala.

Thank you, Chairman. Guatemala has participated actively in the Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations, to which we attach a great deal of importance. As a troop-contributing country and as a Member State of the Non-Aligned Movement, my delegation has made significant efforts during this session of the Committee. We have participated proactively and in good faith in the search for consensus, because we recognize the importance of updating its recommendations so that peacekeeping missions and our blue helmets can fulfill their mandates, carry out policies and actions that are geared towards improving their protection, security and training, and to implement the women, peace and security agenda, peacebuilding and the protection of civilians. That is why we feel extremely disappointed by the situation that we are all facing today. The C-34 is the only forum in which TCCs and PCCs, together with the Secretariat and countries that host peacekeeping operations, have the opportunity to carry out an in-depth review of all issues pertaining to peacekeeping, reaffirming the purposes and principles enshrined in the UN Charter. We are particularly Disappointed that the Special Committee, which in the last 10 years has not been able to adopt its final report on three different occasions, has not been able to overcome the differences as a result of intransigence or unilateral or geopolitical interests, this state of affairs has a negative impact on the collective efforts to ensure that peacekeeping operations can be successful and are aligned to the needs on the ground. distinguished colleagues, the situation that we are facing now means that we need urgently to rethink things. Given the current state of affairs, it is critical that we once again have intercessional discussions on the C-34's methods of work. We hope that in the future all delegations will recognise the critical role that each and every one of the troop contingents play, those that are deployed in the different missions on the ground. They serve under dangerous circumstances and at high risk to fulfill mandates that the Security Council adopts. We should remember that many have given their lives as they went about their work. to help countries torn apart by conflict. That is why, as a minimum, we should respect the commitments that have been reached and the previously agreed language within this Committee. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Guatemala, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the European Union.

Thank you, Chair. Following several weeks of intensive discussions, we would like to thank you and your team, especially the co-facilitators, for the hard work during this year's C34 session. We genuinely appreciate all the efforts that have been made to find common ground between the wide range of views expressed by delegations in the discussions over the last days and weeks. Almost four weeks ago, during the general debate, we pledged that the EU would contribute constructively to the C34 negotiations with the intent to continue improving UN peacekeeping. In this 60th anniversary year of the Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations, we recall its crucial role in guiding and strengthening UN peacekeeping, with the equal participation of women and international human rights at its core, and helping to ensure that the more than 60,000 UN peacekeepers in the field are equipped, supported, and capable of implementing their mandates in the most challenging environments. In spite of constructive engagement from all delegations over the past weeks, it has become clear that the path to consensus was not only extremely narrow, given the diverse views, priorities, and different positions expressed by delegations, but ultimately impossible. We are grateful for your dedication and your team's efforts in bringing positions closer together, and we share your regret that we have not been able to reach consensus on AC34 report this year. In addition, our gratitude goes to the Secretariat and its many experts who shared their valuable expertise and worked to respond to countless questions during the informal consultations. Finally, our profound thanks also goes to the colleagues that supported our discussions from behind the scenes, the Secretariat services and interpreters. We now look forward to continuing our exchanges in a collaborative spirit during intersessional discussions, where we will have an opportunity to consider the working methods of the Special Committee in relation to its annual report. Furthermore, the UN Peacekeeping Ministerial in Berlin will be an opportunity for Member States to not only show their support by announcing substantial pledges, but also to continue discussions about the future of peacekeeping. We reassure you that the EU and its Member States, as always when global peace and stability are at stake, remain steadfast supporters of UN peacekeeping. Thank you, Chair.
I thank the distinguished representative of the European Union, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Denmark.

Thank you, Mr. Chair. Let me start by expressing our gratitude and appreciation for the hard work and efforts by the negotiators, co-facilitators, the Bureau, the co-chairs, and yourself over recent weeks. I also want to thank the Secretariat and the interpreters for their valuable support. You have all done your utmost in the informal consultations and outside them to try to bridge the gaps and find language we could all agree on. Unfortunately, we did not succeed this year, the 60th year for the C-34's establishment. Mr. Chair, UN peace operations continue to be highly relevant, a useful tool and a key element in the international society's efforts for peace and security. We are looking forward to continuing discussions on the development of UN peace operations during our upcoming signature event in the Security Council next week and at the Peacekeeping Ministerial in Berlin. The Thieves 34 is tasked to comprehensively review all issues relating to UN peace operations. That includes making recommendations to all peacekeeping stakeholders. The objective, which we can all agree on, is to improve UN peace operations so that they can deliver on mandates and support the political processes leading to peace and security for the populations in the countries where they are deployed. As UN peace operations today operate in challenging and complex environments, we need to do our utmost to ensure that frameworks, guidelines and conditions take into account the realities on the ground, hand in hand with the UN's overall approach to peacebuilding. Mr. Chair, for Denmark, it is a key priority to support the adaptation and efficiency of UN peace operations and to improve the safety and security of our deployed peacekeepers who are putting themselves in harm's way. We have paid special attention to some important topics. Let me mention five today. Firstly, ensuring timely and effective casualty evacuation. Secondly, support to the uniformed personnel's mental health and well-being. Thirdly, effective use of peacekeeping intelligence and digital platforms like UNITE, AWARE, SAGE. Four, continuously assessing UN peace operations to identify lessons learned and ways to further improve them. And finally, roll-out of renewable energy systems in order to increase resilience and operational efficiency and to decrease the environmental footprint. We will continue to support ensuring full, equal and meaningful participation of women in UN peace operations, also in leadership roles, with the positive effect that follows. As our work in C34 is to improve UN peace operations and to support their work, we could have done so by adopting a comprehensive report with clear recommendations, which could be implemented and which would have a positive effect. To conclude, Denmark regrets that the C34 was unable to reach consensus on a 2025 report, despite almost four weeks of negotiations. Looking forward, we note that recommendations from previous reports are still valid and that implementation will continue, even with no consensus on a report this year. We look forward to the briefings on the implementation of the recommendations in the 24 report and progress made before our next 34 session. Denmark will continue to follow implementation with interest and will continue to provide extra budgetary funding to support the development and improvement of UN peace operations. I thank you, Mr. Chair.
I thank the distinguished representative of Denmark, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Japan.

Thank you, Mr. Chair. As the delegation of Japan and the vice chair of the Bureau, I regret that despite the constructive engagement and effort made by all the delegations, member states have not been able to reach consensus on the C34 report this year. The C-34 has been playing an important role for 60 years, providing policy and operational recommendations to peacekeeping stakeholders with a name to improve the effectiveness of peacekeeping operations in the face of evolving challenges. In this regard, Japan is committed to continue consultations with other member states in the intercessional to consider effective and durable working methods of the C-34 to maintain its significant role. I believe that we can build on the good engagement we had during the session to continue our discussion on the future of peacekeeping operations toward the next annual 34 report, as well as in the occasion of peacekeeping ministerial meeting in Berlin in May. Finally, I'd like to express my sincere gratitude to Ambassador Gort, the chair of the working group of the whole for his leadership. to all the facilitators for their tremendous effort and positive energy they put in to stimulate the discussions, and to the UN Secretariat and the interpreters for their assistance during the session and their valuable work in strengthening the peacekeeping operations. I thank you, Mr. Chair.
I thank the distinguished representative of Japan, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Pakistan.

Thank you, Chair. Pakistan expresses its gratitude to the Bureau, the Secretariat, and you, the Chair of the Working Group of the Whole, for all the efforts during this session of the Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations. Pakistan aligns itself with the statement delivered by Morocco on behalf of Non-Aligned Movement. As one of the biggest troop contributing countries for the last 60 years and a host country to UNMOGIP since 1948, we have a long and profound association with the Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations. This year, by us and other delegations, a lot of effort was put in, many compromises were made and good progress was achieved in the negotiations. However, the efforts of so many came to a nought. We consider these negotiations and recommendations of the Committee invaluable for improving the UN peacekeeping. This Committee embodies the collective ownership of the peacekeeping enterprise by the UN membership. Chair, All countries should engage in a spirit of cooperation to discuss improvements to this important tool, which helps in saving countless lives, protect civilians, and improve lives of millions across the globe. We regret that lack of flexibility and compromise has hindered the important work of the committee and non-adoption of the report. We hope that this approach will be reconsidered. It is important to preserve the work and important recommendations agreed by Member States over years to improve peacekeeping. We cannot afford to lose those gains. We hope that the recommendations will continue to be implemented. We look forward to the intersessional consultations, which should review the working methods of the Committee and agree on practical solutions that can prevent the recurrence of situations such as this year. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Pakistan, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of El Salvador.

Thank you very much, Chairman. El Salvador welcomes the convening of this final plenary meeting of the Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations. We are deeply grateful to Canada as chairs of the Working Group on the Whole, the distinguished delegations of the Dominican Republic, Thailand, Spain and New Zealand as facilitators, and we'd like to thank the Secretariat for their hard work, their support and their commitment during this session. We would also like to extend our gratitude to all of the regional coordinators and the delegates from all of the regional groups and member states who were involved with dedication and a constructive spirit in the deliberations and negotiations that were carried out during this session. My country fully aligns itself with the statement delivered by the Kingdom of Morocco on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement. Mr. Chairman, El Salvador deeply regrets the fact that, in spite of the tireless efforts made by delegations, the Special Committee is not able to adopt a substantive report for this session. The Special Committee remains the only UN forum that has the mandate to review all of the peacekeeping operations issues and how to improve them. It is an inclusive and legitimate forum in which all Member States participate, including those who contribute with police forces and troops and host countries as well. It is a forum in which all Member States can raise legitimate concerns and participate in the quest for improvements to enhance or measures to enhance the role of the organization in international peace and security. That is why we're deeply concerned about the fact that this forum has been paralyzed by national considerations that have nothing to do with peacekeeping. This does not just exacerbate the the inequalities that already exist in decision making in the organization, but it also affects the ability of the organization to fulfill its goals. Mr. Chairman, El Salvador recalls that this special committee has a fundamental role in policies that govern the facilitation of political processes, the protection of civilians in armed conflicts, security, and the protection of peace personnel, promoting and protecting human rights, ensuring women's participation in peacekeeping operations, peacebuilding and sustaining peace, among many other important issues. As has been mentioned by delegations who spoke before me, our collective efforts should not deviate from the goal to broaden and improve the role of the United Nations to achieve these important ends. That is why my country invites all Member States to preserve and work to achieve the valuable agreements that decades of exhaustive negotiations have made it possible to achieve in this Special Committee. Maintaining these agreements is critical to guarantee consistency and the impact of our efforts. In addition, we encourage all Member States to take an active role in the intersessional consultations of the Special Committee. We think that this forum has the potential to maintain the impetus in the key discussions and to transform the entire committee, ensuring that it remains the most legitimate forum for deliberation and decision-making on the matter of peacekeeping. Mr. Chairman, my country strongly believes that the lack of a substantive report for this session should not demotivate us. Rather, it should be a call to action. It should be an incentive for us to redouble our efforts to protect the multilateral approach to peacekeeping and international security. In this, you can count on El Salvador. We will remain committed to UN peacekeeping operations, both in this forum and on the ground. Thank you very much.
I thank the distinguished representative of El Salvador, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Indonesia.

Thank you, Mr. Chair. Indonesia aligns itself with the statement delivered by Morocco on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement. At the outset, Indonesia would like to thank you, Chair, the co-facilitators and all negotiators for the hard work in guiding the negotiation process for the past three weeks, and also to the Secretariat for their support. We echo the disappointment of others that the C34 is unable to adopt the substantive report for 2025. The failure, twice in the period of four years, serves as a stark reminder of the erosion of multilateralism, where its principles of cooperation and compromise should have guided our dialogue in this forum. If this trend continues, we will be on a slippery slope, losing the diplomatic means to find a common ground. Mr. Chair, our peacekeepers are confronting increasingly complex and multifaceted challenges. Given its strategic position and mandate, it is deeply regrettable that this Special Committee, as the only UN forum mandated to review the whole question of the peacekeeping operations in all their aspects, has not been able to lead the discussion on how we could improve the peacekeeping operations to be more fit for purpose. in addressing current and emerging challenges. However, Mr. Chair, moving forward, Indonesia takes note of the decision by this Committee to convene the intersessional discussions to consider the working methods in relations to the annual report. In this regard, Indonesia would like to reaffirm its commitment to play a constructive role and in a good faith to ensure the outcome of the intersessional discussion would ensure a viable solution and for this special committee to take its vital role in reviewing and strengthening all aspects of our peacekeeping operations. I thank you, Mr. Chair.
I thank the distinguished representative of Indonesia, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Mexico.

Mr. Chairman, I would like to begin this statement by thanking you for the sterling work that you have done, as well as your team, and the facilitators of the various chapters of the report of this Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations. Let this opportunity be... used to make our deep gratitude to you all very clear. During the discussions for this committee in February of this year, my country said that peacekeeping operations are perhaps by their very nature one of the most clear examples of multilateralism and an essential tool for the Organization of the United Nations to keep the peace and international security as well. It is therefore regrettable that this year, in spite of the fact that the C-34 has the express mandate to review peacekeeping operations so as to improve them, the lack of agreement and political will have prevented the adoption of a substantive report which would contribute to achieving such a laudable it is critical to recognize that peacekeeping operations are currently going through a range of complex and multifaceted challenges. This is reflected, inter alia, in the high-risk conditions in which both humanitarian personnel and peacekeeping personnel operate. Hence, In addition to this, limitations on human and economic resources remain a critical obstacle as well. The current system has been built up through the collective efforts of Member States over the years. Six decades since this special committee was set up, we are compelled to preserve the agreements we have made and to work on an ambitious agenda with clear goals. Over the 77 years that peacekeeping operations have existed, it is quite clear to us that, if they are to be efficient, we must ensure the full, equal, safe and meaningful participation of women in all peace processes. This includes peacebuilding and peacekeeping. A lot of research has shown that the participation of women in peacekeeping operations has made them more effective. Hence, Mexico will remain committed to fulfilling the women, peace and security agenda. To show this, my country, in line with its feminist foreign policy, has established a national action plan to follow up the implementation of Security Council Resolution 1325. This plan aims to implement specific measures to incorporate gender equality and to mainstream gender equality into all efforts to prevent issues from arising and to keep the peace. We call on all Member States of this organization to join efforts together so as to not allow any kind of backsliding in the agreements that have been made in the domain of gender and on the women, peace and security agenda, particularly given a whole wave of policies and voices that seem to be going in the other direction, which unfortunately we have seen in this committee and in other fora as well. On the potential analysis of the C-34's methods of work, we hope that dialogue will allow us to explore innovative ways to revitalize our work. Consensus, we recognize, is a fundamental aspiration, but it should not be to the detriment of complying with our responsibility or to hamper the substantive improvement in how peacekeeping operations work. Mr. Chairman, we are facing a critical juncture in the history of peacekeeping. This year, 2025, we are seeing the review of this organization's peacebuilding architecture, and it is a timely moment to follow up Action 21 of the Pact for the Future, and in particular to ensure that peacekeeping operations cooperate as soon as possible in planning the transitions with host countries, United Nations teams in the countries, and the relevant national bodies as well. We think that the only option we have is to work together to equip the organization with better infrastructure and tools so that it can respond more flexibly and in a timely manner to the challenges of peacekeeping that are defined and redefined every day. The Government of Mexico is ready to do this. Mr. Chairman, allow me to conclude by reaffirming Mexico's commitment to the purposes and principles enshrined in the United Nations Charter, international law, and the essential principles that underpin these operations. Thank you.

I thank the distinguished representative of Mexico, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of.

Egypt.

Thank you very much for giving me the floor, sir. Mr. Chairman, in my national capacity, I would like to thank you for your tireless efforts during this session of the Special Committee on PKOs. We have seen how hard you have worked over the last few weeks. We'd also like to thank the negotiators and the facilitators for reaching an agreement on the recommendations of the Committee. Mr. Chair, first of all, we align ourselves with the statement of the Non-Aligned Movement delivered by Morocco, Egypt, profoundly regrets the fact that in spite of our participation in the negotiations over the last few weeks and other weeks working within the non-aligned movement in spite of this we haven't been able to adopt a report for the 2025 session we should all think about our ultimate mission which is ultimately to keep the peace and to preserve International Security and we should never overlook these overarching goals. Mr. Chair, this committee remains the UN forum that is responsible for looking into PKOs in all of their aspects. We must therefore all work together. We must work to keep this committee as an area for cooperation and working together to achieve our goals. we must also be mindful of the importance of preserving the what we have achieved over the last few years concerning the principles and concepts for peacekeeping. These principles were the outcome of many years of deliberations and discussions, and they enshrine the wisdom of Member States who wish to ensure that peacekeeping operations can be successful. We are facing a major challenge today, and we are therefore looking to you to facilitate the negotiations that Member States will engage in. This is an opportunity for us to review our methods of work and to redefine the areas where we can improve and to reach practical solutions so that we do not see this state of affairs unfold again. This must allow us to be more effective for peacekeeping operations. Indeed, what has happened during this session of the Committee will have repercussions for years to come. This result could have an impact on all processes within the UN, but we must avoid this happening. We must learn lessons from what has happened on the basis of what we have seen today. We must protect the spirit of working together within this organization. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Egypt, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Sri Lanka.

Thank you very much, Chair. At the outset, let me express my sincere gratitude to the Bureau, the Chair of the Working Group of the Whole, the team of the facilitators and regional coordinators, and secretariat for the support and engagement during the session of the Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations. Sri Lanka aligns with the statement made by the distinguished representative from Morocco on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement. Mr. Chair, Sri Lanka regrets that despite sincere efforts in the negotiation, we were unable to adopt a substantive report due to the circumstances that are beyond the control of C-34. However, we believe finding a way forward is essential as these endeavors, directly or indirectly, have an effect not only on peacekeepers on the ground, but also on the protection of civilians who are living in many conflict-ridden areas. Hence, finding ways and means to navigate through these challenges has become an imperative as peacekeeping has become a decisive tool for global peace. We highly appreciate the significant role played by the Special Committee on Peacekeeping amidst growing complexities. However, we firmly believe that all stakeholders must adopt a holistic approach and assume great responsibility in achieving the objectives of the Special Committee on to ensure lasting global peace. Mr. Shah, we look forward to having more effective and meaningful inter-sessional consultation among Member States to find practical solution that can prevent the recurrence of the situation hindering achieving objectives of the Special Committee. In this context, we believe that it is important to have a framework that ensures unified commitment inclusive collaboration and collective accountability to shared goals that can mitigate the challenges, which will enhance the resilience, adaptability and effectiveness of the peacekeeping. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Sri Lanka, and I now pass the floor to the distinguished representative of India.

Mr. Chair, India aligns with Morocco's statement on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement. At the same time, I would like to convey the following points in support and in my national capacity. But before I do that, I remember more than 4,000 peacekeepers from our countries who have given their ultimate sacrifice for this idea of peacekeeping. We thank the Bureau, the Chair, and the Secretariat for their efforts during the C34 session. We also commend the negotiators, especially the NAM team, for their tireless work. We also deeply regret the inability to adopt the report due to factors which are unrelated to peacekeeping's core mandate. It's crucial that future efforts to enhance peacekeeping efficiency are not impeded by such consideration. We must remember that peacekeeping is a shared responsibility, and staying silent on this issue is detrimental for all. We reiterate that the Special Committee is and should remain the sole UN forum for reviewing peacekeeping operations. We must safeguard it as a space for constructive dialogue, guided by cooperation and compromise. It remains as the primary platform for all of us, the Member States, the troop and police contributing countries and host states to meaningfully contribute to peacekeeping discussions. Preserving gains which have been made in previous years is essential. We must not lose sight of these crucial agreements. In terms of the intercessional consultations, we believe that these consultations should focus on improving our working methods and finding practical solutions to prevent future hindrances to our work. India is committed to constructive engagement and in conclusion, looks forward to supporting the Chair's effort in facilitating these critical discussions. I thank you, Chair.
I thank the distinguished representative of India, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Rwanda.

Thank you, Mr. Chair. At the outset, allow me to join others and express my sincere appreciation to you and the Bureau for your dedication and tireless effort throughout this session. Rwanda aligns itself with the statement delivered by Morocco on behalf of the NAM. Rwanda regrets that consensus could not be reached in this year's deliberations. While differences in perspectives are inevitable, we firmly believe that there is far more that unites us than divides us. As member states, it's essential to build upon previous agreements to preserve our shared purpose. Our focus should remain on the broader objectives rather than allowing minor disagreements to overshadow our collective mission. The primary aim of our discussions must be to strengthen peacekeeping policy, addressing critical areas such as mandate, funding, logistics, training, and safety and security of peacekeepers in increasingly complex operational environments. The question before us is whether peacekeeping will continue to be a vital instrument for global peace and security or a stage for political contestation. At a time when peacekeeping is facing growing threats, such as financial constraints, evolving mandates, we cannot afford for divisions to paralyze the very process meant to enhance these operations. Our disagreements should never come at the expense of those on the ground who rely on our support to fulfill their mandates effectively. This moment, this is a moment for wisdom and responsibility. We must set aside political differences and focus on the real challenges peacekeepers face daily. The security of UN personnel, the effectiveness of missions, and the trust of host communities depend on our ability to find common ground. I urge all delegations to reflect. Are we truly serving the interests of peacekeeping by prolonging this deadlock? Our commitment to consensus must not waver, especially when the stakes are high. We must reaffirm our collective responsibility, not to individual positions, but to the principles and people that peacekeeping is meant to protect. Looking ahead, we must ensure that our report reflects what truly matters. the need of peacekeepers, the expectations of the communities they serve, and the credibility of the United Nations as a force for peace. Since its inception, peacekeeping has embodied multilateralism, prioritizing the needs of host nations over individual interests. Setting rigid red lines will not assist peacekeepers in the field. Rather, it risks setting a harmful precedent. Rwanda encourages delegations to engage constructively with flexibility, understanding and tolerance, and to avoid politicizing the C34 Working Group, which should remain at the expert level. Shifting goalposts during negotiations undermines the credibility of our collective efforts. Mr. Chair, Rwanda welcomes the consensus on holding intersessional discussions to address outstanding challenges. We urge all delegations to refrain from setting rigid conditions, to embrace flexibility, and to safeguard the progress hard won in peacekeeping. I thank you, Mr. Chair.
I thank the distinguished representative of Rwanda, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Canada.

Chair, colleagues. I have the honor of delivering the statement on behalf of Canada, Australia, and New Zealand as the Cairns Regional Coordinator.

As a long-standing contributor to uniting contributing country to the United Nations peacekeeping operations, Cairns recognizes the crucial role played by the committee in strengthening the UN's peacekeeping mandate, the improvement of operational effectiveness, and the guarantee of the security of blue helmets out in the field.

I need to thank the Chair, the Coordinator, and the exceptional team of co-facilitators who worked tirelessly and in good humor to find a way forward. We are so pleased this year to see the strong leadership of women in these roles. CANS will.

Continue its commitment to constructive efforts. We call on all delegations to renew their commitment to dialogue about the future of peacekeeping and the future working methods of the C-34.

We must remember our shared responsibility is to those who serve under the UN flag and to the communities they are mandated to protect. We pay tribute to all peacekeepers, past, present and future. CANS continues to support efforts to strengthen UN peacekeeping and look forward to working collaboratively to find a path forward, including through the upcoming intersessional. In my national capacity, I would like to add a few additional points. While we were unable to reach a negotiated outcome in this session, this Committee remains an important forum to advance guidance and support to peace operations at a time where they face growing complexities and threats. It is also -- it also facilitates the exchange of new ideas and momentum toward much-needed reform. We urge continued efforts to reach consensus and stay strongly committed to preserving the agreed-upon concepts that this committee has upheld for the last 60 years. I also use this opportunity to again thank the chair, the coordinator, and the co-facilitators for their full, equal, and meaningful participation in the Special Committee. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Canada, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Norway.

Chair, colleagues, on behalf of the Norwegian delegation, let me first thank the Chair for handing your task to our full, satisfaction. Similarly, we applaud our co-facilitators. We could feel your disappointment when we reached the conclusion of not having a report this year. Rest assured, that conclusion was despite of, not because of, your excellent performance. Last year, when I gave my statement here, I was convinced that the C34 was about one thing and one thing only, to have a report. So when all feel very disappointed this year, it is easy to think that this was all a lot of work for nothing. I have, however, realized that there is more to C34 than the report itself. Once a year, all our permanent missions must engage on peacekeeping for a couple of months. The same goes for the MFAs and the MODs in our capitals. It gives peacekeeping a high visibility and increased relative importance. We get insight in other positions and thinking. We get a new knowledge and a broader perspective. We might even change our mind on some peacekeeping issues. This all has value on its own. My delegation would like to thank you, our fellow negotiators, for carefully considering Norwegian and other delegations' language even when you did not like that language at all. There is a foundation of professionality and friendliness in these negotiations that we truly appreciate. We look forward to seeing that again in the intersessional discussions. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Norway, and I give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Russian Federation.

Mr. Chairman, I'd like to thank you, all members of the Bureau, and the Secretariat for holding yet another session of the UN Special Committee on Peacekeeping, the C-34. A special word of thanks goes out to the co-facilitators, Carla, Kulapa, Elena, and Angela, for their unswerving efforts and support. We're grateful to all regional coordinators and their negotiating teams for their constructive attitude and their cooperation. Unfortunately, this year, we didn't manage to garner consensus, nor did we agree on a report containing peacekeeping recommendations. The situation clearly demonstrates the need for all states who are somehow linked to peacekeeping to continue working in a painstaking fashion so as to come to a common denominator in this area of high importance for the UN. After all, peacekeeping is the expression of the collective will of states. Against this backdrop, it's important to remember that any discussions about the future of peacekeeping, as well as any initiatives aimed at reforming peacekeeping, should be worked on and discussed here in the Special Committee on PKOs. It is a singular forum, the C34, where all stakeholders are represented, including TCCs and host states, aims to circumvent the collective will of states by imposing in other fora formulas that haven't been duly addressed at the intergovernmental level. Well, no good can come of such an approach. Mr. Chairman, the work that everyone did in good faith over the last few weeks Spending much time on the report, that shouldn't go to waste. We stand convinced that the compromises on a whole host of topics that we reached this year will serve as the foundation for the subsequent report. On our side, the Russian Federation intends to continue playing a constructive role on the C-34. We aim to pursue further dialogue with all interested states so as to come up with mutually acceptable solutions that would allow us to continue improving and strengthening UN peacekeeping operations. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of the Russian Federation, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of China.

Chair, I thank you and your team for the important work done as chair of the working group, with special thanks to the four co-facilitators from the Dominican Republic, New Zealand, Spain, and Thailand for their tireless efforts, and the secretariat for its strong support. China believes that the Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations is the only formal platform for comprehensive review of PKOs, and that the report of the Committee, if adopted by consensus, would play an important role in improving PKOs. China has all along participated constructively in the consultations on the report. Regrettably, despite arduous consultations, members failed to reach consensus on the report this year. Chair, this year marks the 60th anniversary of the Committee, It is also a critical juncture to usher in a new era on the basis of past achievements. At this new historical landmark, we should stay united and work jointly to foster opportunities amid challenges and chart new paths in times of change. It is from this perspective that we welcome the Committee's decision by consensus to discuss the working methods to be used in considering annual reports. We hope that all parties, based on the fundamental principle of consensus, will be able to come up with a common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable model, enabling the relevant work to be more responsive to the new situation and new changes, and enabling a better role by the committee in contributing to the effectiveness and efficiency of PKOs and their smooth and orderly transformation. China stands ready to work tirelessly with all parties to this end. Thank you, Chair.
I thank the distinguished representative of China, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Nepal.

Thank you, Mr. Chair. I align with the statement delivered by Morocco on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement. I extend our sincere appreciation and gratitude to the Bureau, the Chair of the Working Group, all the coordinators and facilitators for their intensive efforts and consultations over the last three weeks of C34 sessions. Unfortunately, we do not have the report today. We could not achieve what we set out for. Nonetheless, we have yet time to reflect on how we can uphold the progress made so far and committee's purposes in the highest spirits. Nepal places high importance to the Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations and its annual recommendations, which update and guide overall aspects of peacekeeping operations. The C-34 has has been an excellent platform for our collective efforts and collaboration for the betterment of peacekeeping operations. As we move forward to pursue intersessional consultations, we are hopeful that we will show much needed flexibility, collaborative ethos, and engage in constructive dialogue. We believe that every missed opportunity opens doors to the possibilities. At last, Mr. Chair, Nepal is fully committed to constructively engaging in the work of this committee to make the UN peacekeeping as an unfailing and useful tool to deliver peace and security in the world. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Nepal, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Thailand.

Mr. Chair, at the outset, I would like to express my sincere thanks to the Bureau, the Chair of the Working Group of the whole, Ambassador Godt, um, all regional coordinators, all the negotiators, and the secretariat, including interpreters, um, for your support and constructive engagement during this C34 session. My special gratitude to my fellow co-facilitators, Angie, Cara, and Elena, as well as Sophie, our C34 coordinator, for your tireless and dedicated efforts these past weeks. Mr. Chair, recent attacks on the peacekeepers and evolving challenges in peacekeeping operations have made the Special Committee work more important than ever. Even though we are unable to reach consensus for this year's substantive report, we must remain committed to put our collective efforts to protect women and men who sacrifice themselves to serve peace and to protect civilians. Thailand looks forward to the upcoming intersessional consultations, where Member States can reflect and discuss on the working methods in relation to our annual report, the report that provides practical and implementable recommendations to ensure the safety and security for our peacekeepers and civilians, as well as to improve the performance of peacekeeping operations. We are certain that with the spirit of cooperation, the Special Committee can contribute for more efficient UN peacekeeping to maintain international peace and security. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Thailand, and I now give the floor to the last speaker on our list, the distinguished representative of the United Kingdom.

Thank you, Chair. Thank you to you, the Bureau, and the facilitators for your leadership and support. And thank you to all the negotiators for your energy, expertise, and creativity. We are, of course, disappointed that we were not able to achieve a report this year. That is always the goal we are working towards. But nevertheless, we are proud of the progress that we were able to make and the valuable conversations that were had over the past four weeks. We have used intersessional discussions in the past to make agreements that allow us to move forward as a committee. The UK is committed to and looking forward to using the next intersessional discussion to work through the challenges of this session and to enable us to bring about a successful outcome next year and in the years going forward to help steer the work of the UN and its member states. The UK underscores its support for UN peacekeeping. We remain committed to working with partners to strengthen peacekeeping's effectiveness and to assure it can adapt to new challenges. Thank you.

I thank the distinguished representative of the United Kingdom. We have no more speakers on the list. Distinguished delegates, once the report just adopted is processed and issued, the Special Political and Decolonization Committee, the Fourth Committee, will resume its work to consider and adopt the report and will also recommend a related draft resolution for consideration by the General Assembly plenary. Members will be duly informed of the dates for the meetings of the Fourth Committee and the Assembly through journal and e-delegate announcements. In the meantime, the Secretariat will upload an advance unedited version to the C34 place on e-delegate as soon as possible. At this stage, I would like to give the floor to Mr. David Harry, Director of the Policy Evaluation and Training Division of the Department of Peace Operations. David, you have the floor. Thank you.

Thank you, Ambassador Goode. distinguished delegates, on behalf of the Secretariat and particularly the USGs of DPO, DOS, DMSPC, I should say DGACM as well, I want to appreciate all the significant time, effort, and commitment invested by your delegations in these negotiations over the last month. And As we've said many times, the strength of UN peacekeeping crucially depends on the consistent and unified backing of member states. And this is why the work of this special committee, which represents a vast majority of the UN's membership, is so crucial in reaffirming member state consensus and delivering the substantive guidance that strengthens our ability to fulfill our mandates. And so if you'll allow me, Ambassador Gort, to express also our sincere regret that despite your best efforts, consensus on a substantive report was not reached this year. Of course, all of us in the secretariat stand ready to continue to support the C34 in its work going forward. Distinguished delegates, six decades after this committee's establishment, as peace gets pushed further out of reach in too many places, Peacekeepers continue to protect the most vulnerable. Our peacekeepers, your peacekeepers, are holding the line and carrying out their mandates in extremely challenging and often dangerous circumstances. Men and women, military, police, civilians. And this in daily practice, I think, really represents multilateralism and global commitment to peace at its highest form. And peacekeeping needs to continue to be strengthened, needs to continue to reform, even while we recognize that it has made hard-fought gains in supporting countries emerging from conflict, in protecting civilians, and fostering stability. But these gains often remain fragile, and continuous work is needed to strengthen the peacekeeping tool in light of current and emerging challenges. And so I'm hopeful that in your upcoming intersessional discussion and beyond, members of this committee will be able to further strengthen its working methods and to ensure this committee can continue to play its crucial role in coming years. Allow me also to acknowledge you, Ambassador Gort, as chair of the Working Group of the Whole, and applaud you on shepherding this committee. Also, as has been mentioned by others, the members of the Bureau, the co-facilitators, the Secretariat is certainly, as I said, ready to continue to support you and appreciate all the efforts that were put in. I also want to thank Sophie Robideau, the Bureau Secretary, for on your first year in this role, being a guiding hand to committee members and the secretariat. I think I would also like to recall that there are many departments in the secretariat that are supporting you, that are with you, and in this cycle, of course, supported in the field and in headquarters. I recall the C34's field mission, the 16 informal briefings that were held, the written answers to your 206 questions. I want to thank all the departments involved, of course, DPO, DAS, DMSPC, but also the Peacebuilding Support Office, the Office of the Victims' Rights Advocate, the Office of the Special Coordinator on SEA, OHCHR, Office of Legal Affairs, Department of Safety and Security, and many others who supported as you needed to provide you the information, and we stand ready to continue to do that. So we're here to continue supporting the committee, and I want to appreciate my team also sitting behind me, particularly Bastian and Judith, and all of those other experts in the departments I mentioned who assisted this year. And thank you for your commitment to peacekeeping. Thank you for that commitment as represented by the peacekeepers who will wake up tomorrow and carry out their mandates. And we stand ready to continue this collective endeavor as we move forward on the part of the Secretariat. Thank you.

Thank you, David, for your ongoing support and for those words. Distinguished delegates, in accordance with the Committee's working methods, the Secretariat will organize a series of intersessional briefings on peacekeeping operations and committee members will be informed of the schedule and topics of these briefings through e-delegate. Before adjourning, I would like to once again thank members of the Bureau for their support and advice, the co-facilitators of the two sub-working groups, as well as all members of the Special Committee for your active participation in the Committee's work this session. Of course, I want to thank Sophie sitting behind me, without whom I wouldn't have been able to do this job. So thank you, Sophie, from all of us. Finally, and on behalf of the Committee, I would like to express sincere appreciation to the Secretariat, including the Department of General Assembly and Conference Management and the Departments of Peace Operations, Operational Support, Management, Strategy, Policy and Compliance, and of political and peacebuilding affairs for their support during this session. I wish you all a wonderful weekend. And on that note, I would like to conclude our 2025 substantive session. The meeting is adjourned.
